question.text: Let the lines <math><msub><mrow><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> be normals to <math><msup><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi></math> and tangents to <math><msup><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>12</mn><mi>y</mi></math> (where <math><msub><mrow><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> are not <math><mi>x</mi></math>-axis). The absolute value of the difference of slopes of <math><msub><mrow><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> is

solution.text:
The tangent to x2=-12y is kx=y+-3k2
Normal to y2=4x is y=mx-2m-m3
⇒k=m & 2m+m3=-3k2
⇒mm2+3m+2=0⇒m=-1,-2 ( m=0 is rejected)
Hence, the difference of slopes is equal to 1
